notes: This source/test traceability contract covers only Umbra's object-instance Request Attribute Value Update and matching Provide Attribute Value Update callback path in the non-installable IEEE 1516.1-2025 development profile. It uses only candidate records exported by the Requirements Lab and does not infer missing IDs. The implementation validates attributes at the requester's currently known object class, groups existing owners, preserves the tag, and rechecks a provider after queueing. A focused production-filesystem regression additionally proves the explicit provider-side callback report appears before callback user code; it does not turn the report into public MOM interaction delivery. The sibling class-designator request form has its own traceability contract. This slice intentionally implements neither regional request forms, automatic provision, an ensuing value-update response, timestamped/retraction behavior, DDM, update-rate reduction, ownership transfer, FOM sharing policy, save/restore, remote transport, packaging, catalog evidence, nor conformance. The linked Catch2 test demonstrates a bounded implementation slice, not full IEEE 1516.1-2025 conformance.
